title: Lights and vessels: the soul in the body, sight in the eye, and the 248 limbs of the King
overview:
Before he can explain the lights of *Zeir Anpin* and its unions, the Mitteler Rebbe opens a five-chapter introduction on lights and vessels. The lights of the *sefiros* are *b'li ma*: real, but not definable, the way you know a person and still cannot say who he is. The vessels are a tangible, defined expression, and through them G-d is revealed to man and conducts a world that seems separate. The four spellings of the Name, *Ayin Beis*, *SaG*, *MaH* and *BaN*, all speak of the vessels.

The body is the *mashal*: brain, heart and liver for *neshama*, *ruach* and *nefesh*; every vessel an inside, middle and outside; 248 limbs of the King. Light in a vessel is like sight in the eye. It changes its nature, from spiritual to physical, and it is limited, as the hand can lift only so much, though a sudden fright shows the soul's power has no limit. Yet the matter is made to fit the form, from its lowest level, like a cup designed from the wish to drink, and so body and soul grow together, day by day, until seventy.

terms.gloss: vessels: the tangible, defined expression of something, like the body for the soul or words for an idea
sefiros without a what: as lights they have no mahus, real but not definable
garments: the ten vessels G-d made to reveal Himself to man and to conduct the world
the spelling out of a letter's name: the yud, alef or hei in between that make the four Names
three rulers: the brain, the heart and the liver, the vessels of neshama, ruach and nefesh
head, middle and end: the inside of a vessel that serves its purpose, the middle that is the vessel itself, the outside by which it is used
the body of the King: the kelim of Zeir Anpin, with their 248 limbs
garments: Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya as the clothes of the body, or thought, speech and action
a change of nature: a spiritual consciousness becoming a physical, measurable process
limitation: the measure the matter of the vessel imposes on the light
matter and form: the matter limits the form, yet is made to fit it
thickening: making an abstract goal more and more tangible until it becomes the form of a vessel

sections.title: From Abba and Ima to Zeir Anpin, by way of a five-chapter introduction
sections.summary: Having explained the lights of *Abba* and *Ima* and their unions, the Mitteler Rebbe turns to *Zeir Anpin* and its unions with *Nukva*. But first come five chapters on lights and vessels in general.

phrases.en: And behold.

phrases.he: אחר שנתבאר דרך פרט קצת בענין אורות דאבא ואמא
phrases.en: After we explained a little bit in detail (so that was only a little bit of explanation) about the lights of *Abba* and *Ima*,
and the way that they joined together,
whether on the inner level or the outer, the external level.
Now,

phrases.he: יש לבאר פרטי ענין אורות דזעיר אנפין
phrases.en: now we ought to be moving right along on to *Zeir Anpin*,
which, the *partzuf* of *Zeir Anpin*, is called *Yisrael* and it's called *Yaakov*.

phrases.he: וכל פרטי היחודים דזעיר אנפין ונוקבה
phrases.en: We should explain the *yichudim* of *Zeir Anpin* with *Nukva*,

phrases.he: שנקרא יחוד ישראל ולאה או יחוד יעקב ורחל כו' כידוע.

blocks.text:
Until now the Mitteler Rebbe explained, only a little, the lights of *Abba* and *Ima* (lit. father and mother), the *partzufim* (statures) of *chachma* (wisdom) and *bina* (understanding), and their *yichudim* (unions) on the inner and outer levels: in *chachma*, *bina* and *daas*, in *chesed*, *gevura* and *tiferes*, or in *netzach*, *hod* and *yesod*. Before that, how they receive from the *mazalos*, from the arms and from the *netzach*, *hod* and *yesod* of *Keser*.

Now we move right along to *Zeir Anpin* (lit. the small countenance), called both *Yisrael* and *Yaakov*; why, he explains later.

Then come the *yichudim* of *Zeir Anpin* with *Nukva* (lit. the female), *Yisrael* and *Leah* or *Yaakov* and *Rachel*. Really there are four combinations, each of *Yisrael* and *Yaakov* with *Leah* and with *Rachel*.

But first comes a five-chapter introduction on lights and vessels; then *Zeir Anpin* in general, a recap of *yichud*, the difference between *Yaakov* and *Rachel*, and only then the *yichudim*. It is five chapters before *Zeir Anpin* comes up again, and ten before its unions with *Nukva*.

sections.title: Lights have no what, vessels are a tangible something
sections.summary: The lights of the *sefiros* are *b'li ma*: real, but not definable, like a person you know but cannot explain. The vessels are a defined, tangible expression, and through them G-d is revealed to man and conducts the world.

phrases.he: אך תחלה יש להבין הקדמה בענין אורות וכלים
phrases.en: but first we have to understand some prerequisite concepts about lights and vessels
in general and in their details.
It's known, this is a very famous saying of the *Zohar*,
that He is one with His life forces;
the life or the soul, that means the lights of this *hishtalshelus*,
He is one with the body;
the organs or the body is a *mashal* for the vessels.

blocks.text:
But first some prerequisite concepts about lights and vessels, in general and in detail.

The famous saying of the *Zohar*, "He and His life forces are one, He and His organs are one," is a *mashal* (analogy) of soul and body. *Garmohi*, the organs, is the body. The life, the soul, means the lights of the *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent); the body is a *mashal* for the vessels.

phrases.he: ומצד בחינת האורות דעשר ספירות בכלל ובפרט
phrases.en: When we're talking about the lights of the ten *sefiros* in general and also for each *sefira*,
then we call the *sefiros* *b'li ma*,
that they are *b'li mahus*, that they don't have a *mahus*, which means that you can't tell me what they are.
like it says,

phrases.he: ולאו מכל אינון מדות כלל כו'
phrases.en: we say that G-d has nothing to do with any of these *middos* at all.

blocks.text: As lights, the ten *sefiros* (the Divine attributes), in general and each one, are called *sefiros b'li ma* (sefiros without a what), *b'li mahus*: they have no *mahus* (what a thing is in itself). You cannot say what they are; they could really be anything; the vessel is what makes it limited and defined.

blocks.title: The birthday present
blocks.text: In chapters 10 and 11, where *b'li ma* first comes up, he compares it to *Echad*. You want to buy somebody a birthday present. You already have the general *ratzon* (will), but you do not know yet what to get him. Asked what, you don't know: it is still just the general light.

**Like it says**, "And He is not any of these *middos* at all": **G-d has nothing to do with any of these *middos* at all**, so His revelation in the *sefiros* is not definable. Only the vessel defines it: wisdom is the vessel, and in it He is revealed as wise, "the wise guy." But what you know of Him from it is not a tangible thing.

blocks.title: Who are you?
blocks.text: You get to know Him a little from His wisdom, His kindness, all these things, but what you know is not tangible. Like a friend you know, as much as you know him, after all your experiences together: asked who he is, you still cannot explain his *etzem* (essence); it is just him. You see him in all kinds of things, a certain style, "a him kind of thing." That revelation of the person is *b'li ma*; the vessel is tangible.

You know a person through what he does, thinks and says. And *b'li ma* does not mean that it is not real, or not known at all. It is the real thing, like a person's talent, which you can appreciate and which is still *b'li ma*.

blocks.title: A home, not a house
blocks.text: Or you want something that is not yet defined. You want a home; you do not want a house yet, just a home. That *ratzon* is not a fake thing; it is the real *ratzon*.

This is what philosophers bother themselves with: what is love, what is truth. They do not want particular examples; they want the light, the real thing. And light has levels: the regular light, and the *etzem or* (the essential light), the revelation of the person. But even the light of the *sefira* itself, the real light of *chachma*, is still *b'li ma*.

What is the real thing of wisdom? You see it in particular instances, but its essence is not tangible; you cannot really define it. Recognizing these things is a human thing. Kindness is not something you could write down on paper: do this and that and you are being kind. It depends on the situation; it is a sensitivity, an attitude of wanting to do good. So with wisdom and understanding: intellect is what you feel is graceful, beautiful, symmetrical, logical and orderly.

blocks.question: What is a working definition of *or*?
blocks.text: Start with *kli* (vessel), which is a lot easier: it has a *ma*. A *kli* is a tangible, defined expression of something. The *or* (light) is the abstract, intangible point behind it: the goal, or what the tangible thing represents, since a tangible thing always represents something.

blocks.question: Is it the difference between *chachma* and *bina*?
blocks.text: Kind of. *Chachma* is often called *or*, and *bina* puts things into *osios* (letters) of *machshava* (thought), which are like *kelim* (vessels). But it is a more general thing. It says *chachma* has no *osios*, but really it has a higher type, not a language: "You're not thinking to yourself a language in *chachma*. You're just picturing things." Its letters are the particular way you think of whatever you are thinking about.

blocks.title: The car you picture
blocks.text: If you are thinking about a car, you imagine a certain car. That car you chose is a *kli*, because you are using it to represent all cars. So a higher level of *kli* can be abstract to a lower level.

So a teacher's words become the students' inner understanding: light to them, vessels to him. Really that is not so: the words are like a *masach* (screen) that the light is *boke'a* (breaks through); they only carry the light.

The *kli* also has *pnimiyus* (an inner side) and *chitzoniyus* (an outer side). But the *or* is the soul and the vessel is the body: "Everything has a soul." That is a better definition. An artist or a speaker can go through the motions, technically right, without the soul: the talent, the feeling, the sensitivity. That is the light.

A lot of times people learn things, parrot them back and pass their tests, but they really don't get it. They have the vessels, the letters, but not the light. A person who *chaps* it (grasps it), even if he does not do so well memorizing for the test, can apply it, explain it and use it. "If you have the light, it's a real thing."

blocks.title: Gemara in Chassidus terms
blocks.text: Rabbi Walters has this problem himself: you have the soul of an idea, but not the terminology the other person is used to. Each culture has its jargon; even within Chabad, *baalei nigleh* (scholars of the revealed Torah) and people into *Chassidus* have their own. Learning with a *baal nigleh*, he explained the *Gemara* in *Chassidus* terms, the *chomer* and the *tzura* (the matter and the form), and it really annoyed the man until he got used to it. Sometimes a very big thing is just saying things in people's words. "You got to know the lingo." The *kelim* are the words.

blocks.title: Getting married
blocks.text: So even having the light is not enough: to bring it over to somebody else, the *kelim* are often very important. Like getting married: personality, character, beliefs and views are the soul; how old, how tall, what they look like, the body. People also care about the body. Have everything good in the soul but not present it in a way people like, and they will not necessarily take it. Some care more about the body, some less.

phrases.en: But when we speak about the *kelim* of the *sefiros*,
then the *sefiros* are a tangible existence. We can say what they are.
and this is what it says,
that G-d made ten garments,
and He called them ten *sefiros*.
to reveal Himself to man,
to conduct the world with them.

blocks.text: So the lights are not tangible. **But when we speak about the *kelim* of the *sefiros*, then the *sefiros* are a tangible existence. We can say what they are.**

**And this is what it says** in the *Zohar*: **G-d made ten garments**, ten *tikunim* (a *tikun* means a garment), **and He called them ten *sefiros*.** These are vessels to reveal His abilities through, **to reveal Himself to man** and **to conduct the world with them**. Through them G-d is known in a tangible way.

Putting something into a vessel is what lets you express it to someone separate from you, as you have to speak to express ideas. And these are the interface of the *hishtalshelus* as *Hashem* set it up: G-d relates to the world through them.

This is what allows the world to seem separate: it is conducted only through these vessels. G-d decided to reveal Himself through the *chesed* (kindness) of *Atzilus* (the world of Emanation), as a creator; that is the light. The vessel, the ability to create, gives our world its meaning as a created entity that seems separate, and connects it to G-d as a revelation of His ability to create. So the vessels of the *sefiros* are the intermediary: the separate, limited world is connected to Him through them, because He chose to reveal Himself through them.

The *sefiros* are in between: limited in one way and infinite in another, so they can reveal the connection between the world and G-d. Not that G-d had to use them. But since *Hashem* wanted a world that seems separate from Him, where through working we find Him, He made it in steps, and one step is the *sefiros*.

He could have revealed Himself in infinite other ways, but He chose these tangible ones. The ability to create from nothing we do not have, so we do not really know it, but we can have a *hasagas hametzius* (a grasp that it exists) of it. Creation itself we know: seeing it, we understand that an ability to create is behind it, and a creator. So we see G-d through creation.

And the world is conducted through them. Your soul is too spiritual to move a physical thing; it has to come into the body and move it with the hand. G-d could just do what He wants, but for the world to seem like a world, it has to run through limited systems that give it a nature and inherent limitations.

"It would blow the cover if G-d would just be doing whatever He wants without some sort of order." So He runs the world by a system and attributes. Even miracles look like a normal miracle: we know what a classical biblical miracle will look like, because the miracle vessel of *Atzilus* looks a certain way. Going through these limitations is what makes the world a world.

sections.title: The four Names are the vessels of the sefiros
sections.summary: The ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus* are called the four spellings of G-d's Name, *Ayin Beis*, *SaG*, *MaH* and *BaN*, and together the secret of the Holy Name. All of this, names and numbers, speaks of the vessels.

phrases.he: וכן מה שכללות עשר ספירות דאצילות נקרא בד' שמות,
phrases.en: And this is also the idea that the *sefiros* of *Atzilus* are called the four names:
The name of 72
is spelled with the *yud* ones: *yud-vav-dalet*, *hei-yud*, *vav-yud-vav*, *hei-yud*.
That's the name that corresponds to *chachma*.
The name of 63
is spelled the same way as *Ayin Beis*, except the *vav*, instead of being *vav-yud-vav*, is *vav-alef-vav*.
represents *bina*.
The name of 45
has *alefs*,
and that represents *Zeir Anpin*.
And then the name of 52,
that is *yud-vav-dalet*, *hei-hei*, *vav-vav*, *hei-hei*, which is really just the letters being doubled.
And that represents *Malchus*.
As is known.

blocks.text: So too the *sefiros* of *Atzilus* are called the four names: 72, 63, 45 and 52. The name *Havaya* can be spelled out in different ways. The *yud* is always *yud-vav-dalet*, but the *hei* can be *hei-yud*, *hei-hei* or *hei-alef*, and the *vav* can be *vav-yud-vav*, *vav-vav* or *vav-alef-vav*. Four of those combinations come up all the time.

*Ayin Beis* (seventy-two) is spelled with *yuds*: *yud-vav-dalet*, *hei-yud*, *vav-yud-vav*, *hei-yud*, which add up to 72; it corresponds to *chachma*. *SaG*, 63, is the same, except the *vav* is *vav-alef-vav*: an *alef*, one, instead of a *yud*, ten, so nine less. It represents *bina*.

*MaH*, 45, has *alefs*, *yud-vav-dalet*, *hei-alef*, *vav-alef-vav*, *hei-alef*: *Zeir Anpin*. *BaN*, 52, has *heis*, *yud-vav-dalet*, *hei-hei*, *vav-vav*, *hei-hei*, the letters just doubled: *Malchus*, as is known.

Rabbi Walters admits he never saw much of an explanation of why. *Kabbala* uses two *meshalim*, the soul and the body, and letters; the *miluim* (spellings out) of the names are the *mashal* of letters. *Chassidus*, and *Shaar HaYichud* above all, explains the soul and the body, the psychology. The details of the letters and spellings he does not see explained much, and he does not understand that system that well. He thinks he knows the general idea, and is trying to figure it out.

The *yud* is the point of *chachma*, so the *milui* of *yuds* is in *chachma*. The *alef* is a *yud* on top, a *yud* below and a line between: a point revealed through a *masach*, a *bekia* (breaking through) of the point as it comes through an interface.

So in *bina*, he guesses, you still see the point intellectually, but its *middos* are given an interface, a definition; the idea is broken up. In *Zeir Anpin* everything is interface: the *middos* come from *chachma* through *bina*, and the entire *chachma* is interfaced into a *midda*.

*Malchus* gives over the *etzem*, *b'helem* (in hiding), but the whole *etzem* comes over; that is why the letters are just doubled. *Likkutei Torah* explains it, on *Chayei Sarah* he thinks, in the first discourse: *Malchus* is called *Me'aras HaMachpela* (the doubled cave) for this doubling, the name *BaN*, *hei hei*, *vav vav*, *hei hei*, where the *etzem* comes over exactly as it is. Doubled without a *memutza* (a middle), it comes over straight, like *yesh me'yesh* (something from something).

blocks.title: Giving a dollar, giving an idea
blocks.text:
Give you a dollar and there is nothing in between: I give it, you get it. But an idea or an emotion you do not get exactly the way I have it. There is a *tzimtzum* (contraction); it comes through as a light that represents it, and you have to extract the point, read between the lines, extrapolate the principle from my example. In spiritual things you do not get the *etzem*: that is *yesh me'ayin* (something from nothing).

So there is a *yud* in between, a *tzimtzum*, or an *alef*, a different *tzimtzum*. In *chachma* you get the *nekuda* (point) as it is; in *bina* and *Zeir Anpin* it comes through an interface, like a *masach*.

phrases.en: In the terminology of the *Zohar*,

phrases.he: כלל העשר ספירות נקרא רזא דשמא קדישא
phrases.en: the whole idea of the ten *sefiros* is called the secret of the Holy Name,
as is known.

phrases.he: הכל הוא רק מצד בחינת הכלים דוקא כידוע.
phrases.en: So all of these things where it speaks about the names and the *gematrios* and all these, these are all the idea of the vessels of the *sefiros*.

blocks.text: **In the terminology of the *Zohar*, the whole idea of the ten *sefiros* is called the secret of the Holy Name**, and all of it is only from the side of the vessels. Wherever it speaks of the names and the *gematrios* (numerical values), it means the vessels of the *sefiros*: the name of 72 is the vessel of *chachma*.
Which level the names mean depends on the context; they could refer to any level of the *hishtalshelus*. Unspecified, you are talking about *Atzilus*, where the main action goes on, the center.

blocks.title: Saying a person's name
blocks.text: *Atzilus* is like the soul in the body. Say a person's name and people picture him: his body with his consciousness in it. Unless I specify his inner self, detached from his body, or the expression of him in his work, which would be like *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, I mean him, the center: *Atzilus*.

So in the *hishtalshelus*: the *sefiros* and *partzufim* usually mean *Atzilus*, unless it specifies otherwise. Speaking of how we see G-dliness in creation, it means *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, and it says "the *chachma* of *Beriya*": G-d's wisdom as we see it in creation. Just say *chachma* and you think of G-d's power of wisdom in the vessel of wisdom, *chachma* of *Atzilus*. G-d's potential for wisdom before the vessel, or what is higher than what we call wisdom, has to be specified, or meant by the context.

sections.title: Three rulers: brain, heart and liver for neshama, ruach and nefesh
sections.summary: The three main systems of the body are the vessels of the three levels of the soul: intellect in the brain, emotion in the heart, biological life in the liver. *Chaya* and *yechida* are above the limitation of vessels.

phrases.en: The explanation of these matters is known, the idea of the lights and the vessels,
on the teaching of the *Zohar*:
there are three chiefs above, there are three supernal rulers, leaders:
the brain, the heart and the liver, and so on,
which are the three vessels for the *nefesh*, *ruach*, *neshama*.
The *neshama*, which is the intellectual part of your soul, goes into your brain.
The *ruach*, which is an emotional part of your soul, goes in the heart.
And the *nefesh*, which means just biological life, is in the liver.

blocks.text: The explanation is known from the teaching of the *Zohar*: *tlas shlitin* (three rulers) above, the brain, the heart and the liver. In the body these are the three main systems, not really organs: the nervous, the cardiovascular and the digestive. They are the three vessels for *nefesh*, *ruach* and *neshama*.

These three levels of the soul go into the general vessels. The *neshama*, the intellect, goes into the brain: "Do I need to explain that? You think with your brain." The *ruach*, the emotions, goes into the heart, which he will explain for those who do not know why.

That is common knowledge, but scientists, and not just scientists, everybody, call it ridiculous. Modern men like to make themselves feel good by making ancient cultures seem stupid: they build the old idea into the most ridiculous construct and laugh at it, "a straw man defense," and never consider that the ancients meant something more intelligent.

sensitivity.reason: Mocks scientists and "the modern men" as making ancient cultures seem stupid with a straw man.
sensitivity.publishable: That is common knowledge, but it is often called ridiculous: the old idea is built into the most ridiculous construct and laughed at, and no one considers that the ancients meant something more intelligent.

blocks.text: So the emotions are in the heart, and the *nefesh*, just biological life, is in the liver, because your liver is what makes you live: it digests your food. You do not need your brain for biological life.

blocks.title: What a person can live without
blocks.text:
In medicine, he says, there are three vital organs a person dies without within minutes, depending which one: the liver, the heart and the kidneys. The kidneys he thinks are the least vital, 15 minutes; the heart like 5; the liver he does not remember.

But a person does not need the brain for physical life at all; on machines he basically does not need it. It is for consciousness, not for being biologically alive like plants: "that's what they call him a vegetable." Using energy and expelling waste needs no brain.

sensitivity.reason: Medical claims given from memory and partly wrong: which organs are the vital ones and how many minutes a person survives without each. His point that the brain is needed for consciousness and not for biological life is kept.
sensitivity.publishable: But a person does not need the brain for physical life at all. It is for consciousness, not for being biologically alive like plants: "that's what they call him a vegetable." Using energy and expelling waste needs no brain.

blocks.text: The main function of life is not in the heart but in the liver: life is using energy, which is digestion. The heart passes that energy along to the other organs, with oxygen so they can burn it. It helps the digestive system "spread the wealth".

blocks.title: The liver takes the poison apart
blocks.text:
They can make an artificial heart, not an artificial liver. In a way it is the smartest part of the body, its function ridiculously complicated. Everything that goes into the bloodstream goes into the liver: food, alcohol, a cigarette, drugs, car fumes. It takes it apart into basic molecules and atoms and puts it back together into useful things, and any poison it alters molecularly so it is not dangerous, and passes it out.

That, he says, is why you can drink alcohol and use drugs "and not die right away," though they are poisons and should really kill you. They harm eventually because sometimes a small percentage, less than 1%, stays behind and damages the liver and the body, or there is too much at once for the liver to clear.

sensitivity.reason: Says the liver is why one can drink and use drugs "and not die right away", with a percentage of harm given from memory; a reader could take it as reassurance about alcohol and drugs.
sensitivity.publishable: They can make an artificial heart, not an artificial liver. In a way it is the smartest part of the body, its function ridiculously complicated. Everything that goes into the bloodstream goes into the liver: food, alcohol, a cigarette, drugs, car fumes. It takes it apart into basic molecules and atoms and puts it back together into useful things, and any poison it alters molecularly so it is not dangerous, and passes it out.
sensitivity.judgmentNote: It explains the liver as the vessel of biological life, but a reader could take "not die right away" and the under-1% figure as reassurance about alcohol and drugs; weigh whether the second paragraph prints.

blocks.title: It takes a lot of brains to make a body
blocks.text:
The liver is also the only organ that regenerates: unless much of it is damaged it fixes itself, and you can live with about 25% of it. Taking food apart and putting it back together into the amino acids, proteins and sugars the body needs, it builds your body from scratch: it is the brain of the physical body's operation. Science cannot duplicate it; it would be really difficult and expensive.

The brain they cannot duplicate, because it is consciousness and that needs a soul; but its physical function is like a computer, wires connected, and that they can kind of duplicate. It is not easy to make a body: "Takes a lot of brains to make a body." These organs are the centers for these aspects of the soul.

phrases.en: But the *chaya*, *yechida*
does not come into the vessels; they do not have a particular organ center.

blocks.text: **But the *chaya*, *yechida* does not come into the vessels; they do not have a particular organ center.** The *chaya*, the inner will and volition, and the *yechida* (the essence of the soul), your inner self, are both in the whole body equally, limited to no particular vessel.

There are physical things that are kind of vessels for them: the *kruma d'avira* (the membrane of air) for the *chaya*, since the senses come from there, and the liquid, it says, for the *yechida*, or some say the skull. But they are not revealed in it. The brain is set up like a computer, so it makes sense as the vessel for thinking; the *kruma d'avira* is not. It is not a proper vessel; it is just *shoreh* (rests) on it, *makif* (encompassing) on it.

And those things are not centralized: the liquid goes through the whole body, not just over the brain, and the *kruma d'avira* covers the whole brain, and he thinks the spine and other parts have similar things. In any case they do not limit it. They are the vehicles it is expressed through in the body, not vessels that limit it, because it is not in them in a *pnimiyus* way.

sections.title: Inside, middle and outside: the 248 limbs of the King and His garments
sections.summary: Every vessel has an inside that serves its purpose, a middle that is the vessel itself, and an outside by which it is used. Nine *sefiros* of nine, times three, plus the five *chassadim*, make the 248 limbs of *Zeir Anpin*, the body of the King; beyond the body are the garments.

phrases.en: And the vessels:
it's composed of head, middle and an end; beginning, middle and end; an inside, middle and an outside,
which is the inner part of the vessel,
the middle of the vessel,
the external part of the vessel.

blocks.text: Now come the basic concepts of vessels. There are the main vessels, the brain, the heart and the liver, for *nefesh*, *ruach* and *neshama*. The *chaya* and *yechida* have no real vessels, no *hislabshus* (being enclothed) in one. And every vessel has three aspects: **head, middle and an end**, **an inside, middle and an outside**: **the inner part of the vessel, the middle of the vessel, the external part of the vessel.**

blocks.title: The cup
blocks.text: As is known, it is like a cup. The inside, the space in the middle, holds the liquid; the outside is where you hold it; and the middle is the actual stuff it is made of. In a way they are one thing, in a way not; the real vessel is the middle. The inside is part of its shape, made to hold something, which is its purpose; the outside lets you hold it, so you can use it.

blocks.title: The handle and the blade
blocks.text:
Some cups have a separate handle, the external vessel: it does not help the cup at all, it just helps you hold it. Sometimes the outside has a special grip, sometimes not. And sometimes the inside, the part that does the function, is special, like the blade of a knife; then the main body gives it stability or value, and then the handle.

So the inner part of the vessel serves the purpose, the higher thing; the middle is the vessel itself, with its properties; the outside is what lets it be used.

blocks.title: The arm
blocks.text: Briefly, since it is explained later: your arm. Its inner part is its connection to the power of movement, the nerves to the brain, so your soul can tell it what to do. The middle is the arm itself, its muscles constructed to move in certain ways. The external part is the way it moves, grabs and does things, the way it relates to what is outside you.

It says something like this of *basar*, *gidim* and *atzamos* (flesh, sinews and bones). The meat is the external vessel: it actually does the movement. The tendons connect the bones the right way so they move the right way; the blood vessels bring blood and oxygen for the energy to move; the bone is what makes it able to do it; and the nerves tell it to do it.

phrases.en: It's known about the 248 limbs of the king:

phrases.he: דט׳ ספירות של בחינת זעיר אנפין
phrases.en: the nine *sefiros* of *Zeir Anpin*,
Nine times nine, 81,
has really three parts to it,
the inside, middle and the outside.
So three times 81 is 243.
And when you add the five *chassadim* that make the body grow, you get 248.

blocks.text: As is known, the King has 248 limbs. Why 248? That is the number of limbs: if you count the bones, and he thinks you have to count cartilage too, like the kneecaps, it is 248. But what is the *cheshbon* (count) of the *sefiros*, upstairs? The nine *sefiros* of *Zeir Anpin*, nine because it is not *Malchus*, have 248 limbs. Why?

Nine times nine is 81: each of the nine *sefiros* is a *partzuf* of nine, without *Malchus*. *Zeir Anpin* starts off with ten, *Nukva* attached, but the *Malchus* of each *sefira* is broken off through the *nesira* (the sawing apart) and built into *Malchus*, its own *partzuf*, as *Chava* was made with *Adam* with two faces and then cut off ("we just had *Parshas Bereishis*"). So nine are left, nine each: 81.

The nine general *sefiros* correspond to nine general organs, as in *Pasach Eliyahu*: the right side of the brain is *chachma*, the left *bina*, the skull *Keser*; then the right arm, the left arm, the torso, the right leg, the left leg and the reproductive organ. And each really has nine: your arm has the upper arm, the middle arm and all your fingers.

And each of those, say your upper arm, has three parts, *rosh toch sof* (head, middle and end), the inside, middle and outside: skin, muscle, veins and nerves, bone, all different layers, in general divided into three. Three times 81 is 243, and **when you add the five *chassadim* that make the body grow, you get 248.**

Usually the five *chassadim* (kindnesses) are the liquids that make the body grow. Here it could mean the ends of the bones that grow, or something; Rabbi Walters is not sure what the Mitteler Rebbe means in the body by the five *chassadim*.

phrases.he: והוא כללות ענין כלים דזעיר אנפין
phrases.en: is the general idea of the *kelim* of *Zeir Anpin*,
which is called the body of the King.

blocks.text: Now comes all about the human body and all this physiology, because it is the *mashal* for the *kelim* of *Atzilus*, the *gufa d'malka* (the body of the King). This **is the general idea of the *kelim* of *Zeir Anpin*, which is called the body of the King**: ten *sefiros*, nine in each, three in each of those, plus the five *chassadim*, 248 limbs, and these are the names. The *nimshal* (what the analogy stands for) comes in the next chapter.

phrases.en: So too, *Hashem* made *levushim* for Himself. He made garments,
So these *levushim*, the *mashal* for that is like *machshava*, *dibur* and *maaseh*.
We'll explain all of this.

blocks.text: **So too, *Hashem* made *levushim* for Himself. He made garments**, whose *mashal* is the garments we wear. Of the two main *meshalim* in *Kabbala*, one is the soul and the body: the worlds before *Atzilus* are the soul, *Atzilus* the body, and *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* the clothes. *Beriya* is the hat, *Yetzira* the shirt and coat, *Asiya* the pants and shoes.

It also speaks of *machshava*, *dibur* and *maaseh* (thought, speech and action), as it says here, a less *megusham* (physical) *mashal*. At the end of the last letter they learned in *Tanya*, the Alter Rebbe says that to understand these things properly you have to take the teachings of the Arizal away from their *gashmiyus* (physicality), their metaphoric connotations: they are written in a very physical way, and you have to figure out the *nimshal*. So these *levushim* (garments) are thought, speech and action.

sections.title: Light in a vessel, like sight in the eye: first, a change of nature
sections.summary: The general model of light and vessel is the soul's power of sight in the eye. The first thing that happens is *shinui hamahus*: a spiritual consciousness becomes a physical process, as intellect in the brain, movement in the body and growth in the plant.

phrases.en: However,

phrases.he: הנה ענין אור וכלי דרך כלל,
phrases.en: now we're going to explain the idea of the light and vessel in general.

phrases.he: הגם שיש בו הרבה אופנים שונים מאד,
phrases.en: Although there are many different types of lights and vessels and ways that they work,

phrases.he: אך כללותו הוא על דרך אור וחיות הרוחני של ראיה רוחנית
phrases.en: the general *mashal* for it is like the spiritual power of consciousness of sight, of vision, the soul's power to see,

phrases.he: כשמתלבש וממוזג בהגשמה בכלי חומר העין
phrases.en: which then is enclothed into the eye, into the physical matter of the eye,
physical sight.
So here there are two components, there's two aspects to this eye-soul thing going on here.

blocks.text: **Now we're going to explain the idea of the light and vessel in general.** There are many types and ways, but the general *mashal* is the soul's power to see, enclothed in the physical matter of the eye. That matter is *memuzag* (mixed), put together so that it can see: clear, with little nerves receptive to light, chemical reactions, the cones and rods and the retina. So the eye is the *kli*, the vessel or the tool, for the soul's power of sight.

The consciousness of sights and perceptions is not physical at all; it is spiritual. There is no physical existence of red and blue; they are psychophysical, as discussed before. Those are the light and the *chayus*, which means consciousness. The eye is the vessel of physical sight.

blocks.title: How the eye sees
blocks.text: Physical sight they can explain: the light hits the lens, which inverts the image and projects it on the back of the eye through a clear liquid, and the retina's cones and rods are receptive to different brightnesses and colors. So your eye has only a certain resolution, something like 288 sensors per millimeter, and certain physical limitations.
**So here there are two components** to this: when your power of sight goes into your physical eye, two things are happening.

phrases.en: The first thing is
it's now changing its nature from a spiritual consciousness to a biological process.
That physical sight can see physical things.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן ברוחניות אור הראיה
phrases.en: On the other hand, it's not so with the spiritual power of sight.

blocks.text: **The first thing is** *shinui hamahus* (a change of nature): **it's now changing its nature from a spiritual consciousness to a biological process**, which scientists and doctors can measure and describe: chemicals sensitive to light that trigger different things.

Scientists only tell half the story, and they make it out to be everything; it does not explain why you see blue. Blue triggers this chemical reaction and yellow that one, and there is something to it, but why in the end you see blue as blue is not a physical thing, and no science can explain why it looks the way it does. "That is totally coming from your soul."

**Physical sight can see physical things**, measurably, both ways: how it sees and what it sees are in the physical world. So you can see cups and bowls and trees and clouds and say exactly what is going on. **On the other hand, it's not so with the spiritual power of sight.** The soul's consciousness cannot see physical things without the eye. "It's just aware of itself."

phrases.en: So too with all the other powers of the soul, like, for example, the power of intellect,
which goes into the vessel of the brain,
until you can actually call it what we know as thinking, intellectualizing, coming up with ideas.

blocks.text: So too the soul's other powers, like the power of intellect in the vessel of the brain. The brain is set up to think, like a computer: its nerves let electrochemical impulses follow all kinds of patterns, each representing a different thing, and ordered differently they represent all kinds of thoughts. Chemicals released by patterns, or stored up to trigger them, are how memory and association work. It is a very complicated vessel, physically a good one for thinking. But the actual understanding is in your soul, "and that's why no matter how good of a computer they make, it will never have consciousness."

**Until you can actually call it what we know as thinking**, *hischakmus*: coming up with ideas, insight and understanding, study, the way it works in the physical brain. As light has to go into your eye and trigger a reaction before you see, the brain works a certain way: it gets a stimulus, analyzes it and makes patterns and associations. That is what we associate with studying or thinking.

phrases.en: And the power of movement,
when it comes out physically in your body,
And the same thing with the power of growth, the spiritual power of growth,

phrases.he: שמורכב ומלובש בצמיחה גשמית בגשם הצומח
phrases.en: which then goes into the physical power of growth, which is a whole physical, chemical, biological process.

blocks.text: **And the power of movement**: spiritually your soul has it, but **when it comes out physically in your body**, it depends on how the body is built, with a certain range of motion. We are not built like flies: they fly and cling to walls, and we can't, and we can't turn our head around backwards. So it is limited to our limbs, but physical: now we can make a physical movement. The soul cannot move physically; its movement is spiritual: it connects itself to whatever it chooses and directs its consciousness there.

blocks.question: Could you fly with a human soul?
blocks.text: Sure, why not? Our soul is not a fly's, but in the power of movement we are the same. That is why *Chassidus* says a *gilgul* (reincarnation) is painful: in a body other than a human's, a human soul cannot think, create or express its emotions properly, "so it feels like trapped."

blocks.title: A human soul in a fly
blocks.text:
But the fly does not have a person's power of thinking in its soul, and its vessel fits it. The human body is made to fit the human soul; a fly's body is not. You could stick a human soul in a fly's body and it would work, but it would be very annoying, like using a butter knife as a screwdriver: you could, but it is frustrating. The ability is in the soul; the body just lets it express it.

Flying and walking are the same power of movement. But creative introspection and philosophical inquiry are a power flies do not have in their soul. With a human brain "it would be a really smart fly, but it wouldn't be like a person."

That is a question of which soul it is. Once a soul goes through *Adam Kadmon* (lit. primordial man) it gets a certain form, a human soul or a fly's soul, and cannot go into any body. Before that every soul is the same: *nishmas kol chai*, the soul of everything.
That is the one aspect of the vessel: the light changes and becomes something that can relate to physical things, because the soul cannot relate to the physical world.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 44 opens by summing up the first aspect, the change of nature, before it reads line 32.

blocks.text: **And the same thing with the power of growth**: the spiritual power goes into physical growth, **a whole physical, chemical, biological process**: chemical reactions, little bacteria that take the nutrients apart and make them into different things, the light and the chlorophyll, photosynthesis.

We do and we don't. As chapter 1 explains, you cannot get the depth without the length and the width. You always start with the length, a *mashal*, a practical, tangible example you can know. The depth, the light, is abstract, *b'li mahus*; from the particular example you extrapolate it.

So we know the idea of intellect, of seeing, the spiritual concept behind them, by seeing it in particular examples. Growth we understand as separate from the process that makes it work, because it could work differently, and so what? The physical process is just a means, a tool that lets growth exist. The carbon, the light, the nitrogen, the water, the oxygen and the carbon dioxide are really irrelevant to the real thing of growth: something that builds itself, multiplies itself and makes itself bigger.

blocks.title: Why does a tree grow?
blocks.text:
Still there are two questions. When a tree grows, where does it think it is going? They can explain how it grows, the light and whatever, but why? There is an inherent *ratzon* that makes it want to grow. That is what they call *teva* (nature): a *ratzon* higher than reason and knowledge, wanting it for no reason. That property is not physical; it is a spiritual soul, a drive enclothed in the physical world that becomes its nature, and has no physical explanation.

Whenever they say nature, that is what they mean: something beyond the physical world that they cannot explain, just the way it is, and they do not realize the philosophical implications of the word. "Science doesn't tell you why, it just tells you how."

But the main point: the concept of growth will not grow particular plants; the physical power of growth will. That is the one *inyan* (matter): it goes from spiritual to physical, it changes its *mahus*.

sections.title: Second, the vessel limits and measures the light
sections.summary: The second thing a vessel does is limit: physical sight reaches only so far, the brain can hold only so much, the hand can lift only so much. The spiritual power itself has no limit, as a sudden fright shows.

phrases.en: The second thing that goes on when the light goes into the vessel
when it goes into the vessel, the vessel has certain limitations that it imposes on the power, on this light. So now it is limited according to a certain way, as measured.
It's like physical sight:
you can only see up to 60 miles.

blocks.text: **The second thing that goes on when the light goes into the vessel** is the *hagbala* (limitation) and measure in its matter: **the vessel has certain limitations that it imposes on the power, on this light.** Now it is limited, measured. **It's like physical sight: you can only see up to 60 miles.**

blocks.question: What does "only up to 60 miles" mean? We see the stars and the Sun, and from a high enough mountain farther than 60 miles.
blocks.text:
He is not sure exactly. It probably has to do with the eye's limited number of sensors: far enough away, for a given size, the light from something falls between the sensors and you do not see it at all.

On second thought, what he thinks he figured out is that it means the maximum depth perception. Beyond a certain distance everything seems flat, like the horizon, a backdrop; you cannot tell which mountain is farther. You judge depth by the distance between your two eyes and a couple of other tricks, and far enough away they stop working: the Sun and the Moon look the same distance away. The main thing is that there are physical limitations to the power of sight.

Which limitation he means, it does not say explicitly; one can only try to figure it out. But that is the point: science books and doctors will tell you all the limitations of physical sight. The eye is receptive to a very narrow wavelength, a tiny part of the electromagnetic spectrum, and to only certain colors and brightnesses. It takes a picture only every sixteenth of a second or something, because each time light triggers the chemical reaction that makes you see, it takes time to reset.

phrases.he: וכן ענין התחכמות ותנועת הגשם, מתפשטים בהגבלה מצומצמת
phrases.en: So too with your intellect and your movement, that when they become in the physical vessel of your body, they are limited.
They are specifically very limited.
And then there's a certain point where they will fail, your ability was used up.

phrases.he: כמו שתקצר גשם השגת כלי המוח
phrases.en: Like sometimes your brain just can't understand,
and its ability will just be used up because the vessel is not big enough.

blocks.text: **So too with your intellect and your movement**: in the physical vessel of the body **they are limited**, *davka* (specifically) very limited, **and then there's a certain point where they will fail**. **Sometimes your brain just can't understand**, its ability used up **because the vessel is not big enough.**

You have to develop your brain; it is like a muscle, and exercise makes it better at thinking. An idea can be too complicated for it, until you exercise it to make it finer, sensitive enough to handle it. There can be too much information at once, and there is how long you can think, your attention span. These are physical things.

Little kids have less brain capacity than someone older, and developing parts of the brain makes a person better in those areas; it is physical. And thinking too hard without rest can hurt a person: he does not know the medical term, but they can have a nervous breakdown, "kind of fry their brain." The brain needs to rest, sleep and do different things to reset.

sensitivity.reason: A medical claim he says he cannot name (thinking too hard can cause "a nervous breakdown" and "fry their brain"), close to advice a reader might act on.
sensitivity.publishable: Little kids have less brain capacity than someone older, and developing parts of the brain makes a person better in those areas; it is physical. The brain needs to rest, sleep and do different things to reset.

phrases.he: וכן יוקטן ויופסק כח תנועה הגשמית שמכח היד, בפעולה או בהגבהת משאוי וכהאי גוונא
phrases.en: So too, your power of movement is too small sometimes, and it will stop: when you're doing something, eventually your hand gets tired or just can't do it, or something is too heavy for it to lift, and you just can't do it.

blocks.text: **So too, your power of movement is too small sometimes, and it will stop**: your hand gets tired, or something is too heavy to lift. That is the limit of the moving power: there are ways you cannot move, and you have only so much strength, you can move only so fast and so hard.

phrases.he: (מה שאין כן מצד עצם כח הרוחני של המניע התנועה,
phrases.en: On the other hand, this actual spiritual power of movement
does not have any limitation, and it will never stop, will never run out.

phrases.he: וראיה מהגבהת משא כבד הבא בבהלה פתאומית, ביתר הרבה מכחו,
phrases.en: And the proof for this is when a person has a sudden scare, and they lift something that's much heavier than they could really lift,
which is because of the *makif*: the soul forces the body to do more than it can really do.

blocks.text: **On the other hand, this actual spiritual power of movement does not have any limitation, and it will never stop, will never run out.** The proof: in a sudden scare a person lifts much more than he really could, because the *makif* (encompassing light) of the soul forces the body. There the essential power of movement is kind of revealed.

blocks.title: Feats in a fright
blocks.text: How exactly, he does not know. But there are all these stories of people who did crazy things, in wars and such: jumped over huge things a person normally could not, or fit into spaces too small for them, as if "they shrunk their body a little bit." Normally that is beyond the body's ability.

The soul has much greater control over the body than is normally revealed, and it forces the body to comply with its *ratzon*, like a miracle; and the body really could do it. The source of miracles, he explains later, is the level of the *makif*, and "the actual matter is stupid and it doesn't care." Water does not care whether it flows or stands up like a wall, as when the sea split; it does whatever it is told. So the body does whatever the soul tells it, and in big trouble, with a huge *ratzon*, the soul reveals this essential ability, a miracle on the body.

It depends how high you go: the deeper, the more limitations are lifted; deep enough, you could really do anything. You see it even with hypnosis: the deeper you bring somebody into his subconscious, the more amazing things you can get him to do.

blocks.title: Faith healing and placebo
blocks.text:
And there are deeper and deeper levels. That is also why faith healing and such work: at a certain level your soul can make your body fix itself and work however it wants. A person is sick, he says, because the soul kind of stopped caring and let the body deteriorate; tap a deeper level and the soul can make it fix itself, the deeper the more miraculous, even instantaneously.

There is placebo, and more than placebo: a psychic healer or some spiritual guy, which works only because they believe in it. All stuff has an element of that. Even regular medicine is not guaranteed to have an effect; your body reacts to it in a way that comes from your soul, not purely physically. It is more or less *meluvash b'teva* (enclothed in nature), but either way it is within nature, and either way it is really above nature. It depends how far you want to go.

sections.title: Matter and form: the matter fits the form, made from its lowest level
sections.summary: Matter both changes the form's nature and limits it, yet it is made to fit the form: the vessel comes from the thickening of the spiritual form, from its lowest level, as the design of a cup comes from the wish to drink. So the lowest level of growth, life, intellect and sight goes into the plant, the blood, the brain and the eye.

phrases.he: וכך הוא כל ענין חומר וצורה
phrases.en: This is the whole idea of a *chomer* and a *tzura*.

phrases.he: שהחומר, מלבד שהוא בא בשינוי המהות,
phrases.en: Besides that when you put it into matter, it changes from spiritual to physical,
it also limits the form.

blocks.text: **This is the whole idea of a *chomer* and a *tzura***, *chomer v'tzura* (matter and form): whenever you put something into a form, it limits it. Besides changing from spiritual to physical, **it also limits the form.** Make a cup and you have one particular example of a cup, though you could make different cups. It is always limited.

phrases.he: אבל החומר הוא מעין ודוגמת הצורה,
phrases.en: But nevertheless, the matter is made in a way that is according to the form, so it fits the form,
like the vessel, the eye: the matter of the eye is actually built in a way that's good for seeing,
and the vessel of the mind is made, the brain is made like a computer.

blocks.text: **But nevertheless, the matter is made in a way that is according to the form, so it fits the form.** A cup is made to be a cup. The eye is built to be good for seeing; it has to be clear, and a video camera has to be made kind of like the eye, or else it won't work. **And the vessel of the mind** is made like a computer, fit to think.

phrases.he: אבל החומר נעשה מהתעבות והגשמה של הצורה הרוחנית,
phrases.en: Because the matter is made, not the actual stuff, but the form of the matter is made from the thickening and the materializing of the spiritual form,
from the lowest levels of the spiritual form comes the physical form.

blocks.text: **The matter is made, not the actual stuff, but the form of the matter is made from the thickening and the materializing of the spiritual form.** You thicken an abstract goal into something tangible and physical, the form of the vessel: your desire to drink water is the form of the cup.

blocks.title: Designing a cup
blocks.text: From that desire, given the way water works, you figure out that you need something that holds water: certain materials do and some do not, and it cannot have holes. The shape and material of the cup start to become defined, partially materialized in your mind: something watertight and practical. Then you need a way to hold it, a handle, or the outside has to be like one. Looking at the abstract goal within the limitations of the world around you, you get a picture of the cup; add aesthetics, that it should match your kitchen, and you have a pretty good idea of what you are looking for.

blocks.title: The mug and the wine glass
blocks.text: Then it depends what you want it for, hot or cold. A mug is good for hot things, because ceramic insulates; a glass is not, because the outside gets very hot and it can ruin the glass. Wine glasses are made for wine: the stem keeps your hand from warming the wine and dirtying the glass, so you can see the wine's color and how clear it is, and keep it a little chilled. So the form of the cup follows the light, the *ratzon* you want to accomplish, and the matter is made a tool to the specifications you need.

But abstract considerations differ from practical, circumstantial ones, as in chapter 15, or a house and a home: an inner desire becomes a *ratzon murkav* (a composite will). That is how from the *hisabus* (thickening) of the light comes the vessel. The eye's form fits the power of sight: sight has certain specifications, so in the physical world the eye has to be clear, or else it will not work, and sensitive to light. That defines how the eye has to be built.

**From the lowest levels of the spiritual form comes the physical form**: you make it more and more particular and tangible, until it is particular enough to make an actual physical thing that fulfills the purpose.

phrases.en: So, for example, from the lowest levels of the spiritual concept of growth,
that becomes the source of the physical growth.

phrases.he: וכמו סוף של חיות הרוחני דנפש, מלובש בדם,
phrases.en: or like the lowest level of the consciousness of the soul goes into the blood,

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב כי הדם הוא הנפש כו'
phrases.en: like it says, that the blood is the soul.

blocks.text: **For example, from the lowest levels of the spiritual concept of growth**: growth exists far more abstractly than plants growing from dirt, but its most tangible kind **becomes the source of the physical growth.** To work it has to take a certain form, and that is why physical growth has a certain form.

**Or like the lowest level of the consciousness of the soul goes into the blood**, the power of movement, **like it says, that the blood is the soul**: only what of the soul can show in the body's energy, the most external, most defined application of the spiritual idea of movement.

phrases.he: וכך סוף המדריגה של אור השכל הרוחני מתמזג בחומר כלי המוח,
phrases.en: And the same thing with the lowest level of intellect that can go into the brain,

phrases.he: וכן סוף הגשמה דרוחניות הראיה ממוזג בחומר העין
phrases.en: and the lowest level of sight goes into the eye.

blocks.text: **And the same thing with the lowest level of intellect that can go into the brain, and the lowest level of sight goes into the eye**: the consciousness itself does not go into the body. The brain has no consciousness of thinking or creative ability; the spiritual power's form is represented physically only in its most external parts, and the more spiritual parts stay in the realm of spirit.

sections.title: Body and soul grow together, day by day until seventy
sections.summary: The matter grows with the form: the body becomes a better vessel as the soul's powers mature, and using a power makes the body grow for it. Both take time, day by day, until full maturity at seventy, which is why the Torah sets ages and why one stands up for the old.

phrases.en: Therefore we find

phrases.he: שבכל מקום באין הגדלת החומר עם הגדלת הצורה כאחד ממש
phrases.en: that the body and the soul grow together.

phrases.he: כמו בהגדלת חומר כלי הגוף, שנגדלים ביחד עם גידול אור וחיות הצורה הרוחניות,
phrases.en: Like the body: as you get older, your body grows and develops, at the same time you mature emotionally, intellectually, and your strength gets bigger.

phrases.he: כמו גידול הכנת חומר המוח לפי ערך גידול האור והצורה של השכל,
phrases.en: Like the development of the brain according to the development of intellect,

phrases.he: שכאשר יגדל התינוק ויצמח אור שכלו ברוחניותו, ממילא יצמח כלי הכנת מוחו
phrases.en: as a child grows and develops mentally, matures, at the same time the brain matures physically.

blocks.text: **Therefore we find that the body and the soul grow together.** **As you get older, your body grows and develops, at the same time you mature emotionally, intellectually, and your strength gets bigger.** It is not a coincidence; it has to be. As the body grows it becomes a better vessel. The *or* is there, but the vessel needs to become better to hold the light better.

But it works both ways. As the body develops it can hold more light, and when you use it more, it grows: exercise and your muscles get bigger. Using a power shows a *ratzon* for it and brings that light in. Every time you do something with your body, your soul shines a light into it that refines it into a better vessel for that light, and the more you do it, the more the body builds itself to conform to it.

So exercise makes you stronger, only in the type of exercise you do, and thinking a lot makes you smarter in the kind of things you think about. The body is simple matter; it conforms to whatever desire the soul expresses through it, to be as good a vessel as it can. It develops some on its own, opening greater potential, and the more you push yourself, the more it develops.

**Like the development of the brain according to the development of intellect**: **as a child grows and develops mentally, matures, at the same time the brain matures physically.** It works both ways: the brain matures physically, and thinking more makes it develop more.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב ימים ידברו ורוב שנים כו'
phrases.en: that days speak and many years bring,

phrases.he: שנגדל הכלי עם האור יום יום עד ע' שנה,
phrases.en: that every single day the vessel develops along with the light, and they both develop together until at 70 years old

phrases.he: שבא לכלל גדלות המוחין כידוע ודי למבין:
phrases.en: you reach complete intellectual maturity, and the brain is completely physically mature also.

blocks.text: As it says, **days speak and many years bring**, he thinks, *de'ah* (knowledge), or something like that: just going through life your abilities develop, both because the body develops and because you use it, hand in hand. **Every single day the vessel develops along with the light** until at 70 years old you reach complete intellectual maturity, and the brain is physically mature too. And that is just the brain.

If they had used their brain more, maybe they would be better. But no matter how much you think, it takes time. That is why the Torah sets ages: *bar mitzva*, 20, six for *chinuch* (education), nine. Even a *Rebbe*, really smart and mature physically and spiritually, is not *bar mitzva* until 13; and at 13 without two hairs he is not *bar mitzva*, because you need both. Every single day more of your soul comes out: regardless of effort, you experience more and see more situations, and you mature every day just from the process of life: that is the way G-d set it up. So without two hairs, the body not yet a proper vessel, he is not *bar mitzva*; and with two hairs before *bar mitzva* he is not either, because you need the time. Full maturity needs both together.

Effort makes you more mature, but only within what that age allows: "a 20-year-old is never going to have the same depth of maturity as a 70-year-old." That is why the Torah says to stand up for somebody old, even someone not Jewish, even someone not smart: from so much life he feels the essence of things more. That is the *or* and the *kli*: time brings in more light, and the body develops with it. You need both.

reviewQuestions.question: What does it mean that the lights of the *sefiros* are *b'li ma*, and why does that not mean they are not real? Use the example of knowing a person.
Why did G-d reveal Himself and conduct the world through the vessels of the *sefiros*, and what would "blow the cover"?
How are the four Names spelled out, and what does the doubling of the letters in *BaN* say about *Malchus*?
What are the inside, middle and outside of a vessel, and how does the count of 248 limbs come out?
What are the two things that happen when the soul's power of sight goes into the eye?
How does designing a cup show that the vessel is made from the thickening of the light, and why do body and soul grow together until seventy?

notes.text: Unlike chapter 10, these classes have at least one student. Rabbi Walters addresses him by name ("it's just Shmuel", 39 w986-997; 40 w2151-2166) and mentions sitting next to him in 770 (39 w947-966). Two student questions are heard in the transcript (39 w1538-1544, "A working definition when we say or?"; 39 w1635-1646, "is it the difference between chachma and bina?") and are kept as question blocks. Elsewhere he answers questions that are not heard ("Yeah, He could have revealed Himself in infinite other ways", 40 w554; "No, it depend, it would depend on the context", 40 w2070; "Yeah, there is a kind of...", 41 w1472; "Well, we do and we don't", 44 w118; "if they would have used their brain more", 46 w1080). Those answers are written as explanation or keyPoint blocks, without inventing the question. The one exception is "Yeah, sure. You could fly with a human soul. Why not?" (43 w1895-1913), which repeats the question, so it is a question block with askedBy student.
The two passages that named the student (Shmuel) were once flagged private; they are now written without the person (see the Personal details note) and carry no flag.

Medical remarks given from memory are kept as he said them and flagged health-or-legal: three vital organs "the liver, the heart, and the kidneys", kidneys 15 minutes, heart about 5 (41 w399-472), which is not standard medicine (the brain and lungs are usually named; the kidneys are not survived without for minutes so much as days, with dialysis much longer); that a person does not need a brain to live (41 w480-527); the liver and alcohol and drugs (41 w759-1032); "fry their brain" (44 w1724-1798). Faith healing and psychic healers (45 w547-892) were flagged too, until the reviewer removed that flag (below). A reviewer should check the publishable texts.

Line 21: he reads it (42 w1165-1179) and explains it with the arm (42 w1180-1378). "Three times nine times nine" has no English of his own; the phrase ending "shebakelim" cites "has really three parts to it" (42 w1317-1322), inside the explanation. Lines 19-20: the phrases keep only the words that render the Hebrew ("the nine sefiros of Zeir Anpin", "Nine times nine, 81"); his explanations after them are in the blocks. Line 38 ("from the limitation of the moving power") is read with line 37 and has no English of its own; the block paraphrases it. Line 49's second phrase cites "That's why the body and the soul grow together" (46 w366-376), the sentence after his reading. Line 24's second half ("from which souls fly out"), line 13's "bilvad" and the end of line 43 ("v'cha'hai gavna") are read without English and keep their Hebrew alone. Line 33's middle is read in Hebrew only (44 w851-856).

Line 23: the alignment marks the line at 43 w61, but he starts reading at w59 ("דכולהו כלילן", the machine's hearing). He says each vessel "has ראשי תיבות" (43 w97-115), surely rosh toch sof misheard; the block says three. In 40 w1579-1588 he says that in Zeir Anpin "everything is in a milui now of yud"; the context (the alefs of MaH) suggests he meant alef. That sentence is left out of the block.

Sources as he gives them: Likkutei Torah "on I think Chayei Sarah, the first maamar", on Me'aras HaMachpela and the doubled letters of BaN (40 w1625-1722); "recently in Tanya, right at the end of the last igeres we were doing" (43 w314-373), on taking the Arizal's teachings away from their physicality; Pasach Eliyahu for the nine organs (42 w1180-1251); "Chassidus" on why a gilgul is painful (43 w1950-2008); the Zohar for "tlas shlitin". Left as he said them.

"Going back to like the ט״ו" (45 w1797-1836), next to the house and home and ratzon murkav: written as chapter 15. The terms ratzon murkav and house and home are from chapter 16 in this series, so he may have meant 16 or an earlier class; check the audio.

"Days speak and many years bring, I think, what a de'ah or something like that" (46 w946-984): Job 32:7 reads "days should speak, and the multitude of years should teach wisdom". The block keeps his "he thinks, de'ah". He also says "we just had Parshas Bereishis" (42 w1052-1111), which dates class 42 to the week after Bereishis.

Lines 7-8: he says the purpose of the ten tikunim is "to reveal Himself to man" (40 w105-109); laachaza'a is literally "to show". Kept as his English. "The sefiros are a tangible existence" (40 w25-40) renders "metzius davar ma".
Review (2026-11-23): the flag on faith healing (45 w547) was removed by the reviewer: printed as said.
Personal details (2026-11-23): blocks that named a student, his family or the teacher's family now make the same point without the person (STYLE.md, People in the class).
